p0.original: Bounties upon exportation are, in Great Britain, frequently petitioned for, and sometimes granted, to the produce of particular branches of domestic industry. By means of them, our merchants and manufacturers, it is pretended, will be enabled to sell their goods as cheap or cheaper than their rivals in the foreign market. A greater quantity, it is said, will thus be exported, and the balance of trade consequently turned more in favour of our own country. We cannot give our workmen a monopoly in the foreign, as we have done in the home market. We cannot force foreigners to buy their goods, as we have done our own countrymen. The next best expedient, it has been thought, therefore, is to pay them for buying. It is in this manner that the mercantile system proposes to enrich the whole country, and to put money into all our pockets, by means of the balance of trade.
p0.zh: 在大不列颠,出口时的利润经常向国内工业特定分支的产品申请,有时甚至给予。 通过他们,我们的商家和制造商被假扮成能够比外国市场上的对手便宜或便宜地出售他们的商品。 据说,这样,出口的数量将增加,贸易平衡因而更有利于我们本国。 我们不能像我们在国内市场所做的那样,使我们的工人垄断外国。 我们不能强迫外国人购买他们的货物,就像我们自己同胞所做的那样。 因此,人们认为,下一个最佳时机是支付购买费。 正是以这种方式,商贸制度提议通过贸易平衡来丰富整个国家,并将资金投入我们所有的口袋。

p1.original: Bounties, it is allowed, ought to be given to those branches of trade only which cannot be carried on without them. But every branch of trade in which the merchant can sell his goods for a price which replaces to him, with the ordinary profits of stock, the whole capital employed in preparing and sending them to market, can be carried on without a bounty. Every such branch is evidently upon a level with all the other branches of trade which are carried on without bounties, and cannot, therefore, require one more than they. Those trades only require bounties, in which the merchant is obliged to sell his goods for a price which does not replace to him his capital, together with the ordinary profit, or in which he is obliged to sell them for less than it really cost him to send them to market. The bounty is given in order to make up this loss, and to encourage him to continue, or, perhaps, to begin a trade, of which the expense is supposed to be greater than the returns, of which every operation eats up a part of the capital employed in it, and which is of such a nature, that if all other trades resembled it, there would soon be no capital left in the country.
p1.zh: 允许给予这些贸易分支的财富,只有没有这些财富,才能继续。 但是,商人可以以代替他的价格出售其商品的每一个贸易分支,只要有股票的普通利润,即用于准备和送销的全部资本,就可以在没有赏金的情况下继续出售。 每个这样的分支显然都与所有其他贸易分支处于一个水平,这些分支都是在没有收益的情况下进行的,因此,它们不能要求一个以上的分支。 这些贸易只要求有收益,在这种贸易中,商人必须出售他的商品,其价格与普通利润一样,不能取代他的资本,或者他必须出售这些商品,而卖价却低于他送去市场的实际成本。赏金是为了弥补这一损失,鼓励他继续或也许开始一项贸易,其中成本应该大于回报,其中每个业务都消耗了其中一部分使用的资本,这种性质是,如果所有其他贸易都类似,那么该国很快就没有资本了.

p2.original: The trades, it is to be observed, which are carried on by means of bounties, are the only ones which can be carried on between two nations for any considerable time together, in such a manner as that one of them shall alway's and regularly lose, or sell its goods for less than it really cost to send them to market. But if the bounty did not repay to the merchant what he would otherwise lose upon the price of his goods, his own interest would soon oblige him to employ his stock in another way, or to find out a trade in which the price of the goods would replace to him, with the ordinary profit, the capital employed in sending them to market. The effect of bounties, like that of all the other expedients of the mercantile system, can only be to force the trade of a country into a channel much less advantageous than that in which it would naturally run of its own accord.
p2.zh: 需要指出的是,通过慷慨进行的交易,是两国之间任何相当长的时间内唯一可以共同进行的交易,其方式是其中一方会走远并经常输掉,或出售其货物,其价格低于将货物送上市场的实际成本。 但是,如果赏金没有向商人偿还他本来会损失的货价,那么他本身的利益将很快迫使他以另一种方式使用他的股票,或者找到一种交易,在这种交易中,这些货价将用普通利润代替他,也就是用来将货价送到市场的资本。与商贸制度所有其他权宜之计一样,好处的作用只能是迫使一国的贸易进入一个比它自然会自行经营的渠道更不有利的渠道。

p3.original: The ingenious and well-informed author of the Tracts upon the Corn Trade has shown very clearly, that since the bounty upon the exportation of corn was first established, the price of the corn exported, valued moderately enough, has exceeded that of the corn imported, valued very high, by a much greater sum than the amount of the whole bounties which have been paid during that period. This, he imagines, upon the true principles of the mercantile system, is a clear proof that this forced corn trade is beneficial to the nation, the value of the exportation exceeding that of the importation by a much greater sum than the whole extraordinary expense which the public has been at in order to get it exported. He does not consider that this extraordinary expense, or the bounty, is the smallest part of the expense which the exportation of corn really costs the society. The capital which the farmer employed in raising it must likewise be taken into the account. Unless the price of the corn, when sold in the foreign markets, replaces not only the bounty, but this capital, together with the ordinary profits of stock, the society is a loser by the difference, or the national stock is so much diminished. But the very reason for which it has been thought necessary to grant a bounty, is the supposed insufficiency of the price to do this.
p3.zh: 《玉米贸易区》的天才和知情作者非常清楚地表明,自从首次确定对玉米出口的赏金以来,出口的玉米的价格,其价值适中,已经超过了进口的非常高的玉米的价格,其数额远大于该期间支付的全部丰收。 他认为,根据商贸制度的真正原则,这明确证明这种强迫的玉米贸易有利于国家,出口的价值远远超过进口的价值,远大于公众为出口而花费的巨额费用。 他并不认为这种特别的开支,或赏金,是玉米出口真正使社会付出的代价中最小的一部分。 同样,还必须考虑到农民在养殖过程中所雇用的资本。 除非玉米的价格,在外国市场销售时,不仅取代了赏金,而且这种资本,加上股票的普通利润,否则社会就因为差额而成了输家,或者全国股票被大大缩减了. 但是,之所以认为必须给予赏金,其根本原因,是被认为没有足够的代价来做到这一点。

p4.original: The average price of corn, it has been said, has fallen considerably since the establishment of the bounty. That the average price of corn began to fall somewhat towards the end of the last century, and has continued to do so during the course of the sixty-four first years of the present, I have already endeavoured to show. But this event, supposing it to be real, as I believe it to be, must have happened in spite of the bounty, and cannot possibly have happened in consequence of it. It has happened in France, as well as in England, though in France there was not only no bounty, but, till 1764, the exportation of corn was subjected to a general prohibition. This gradual fall in the average price of grain, it is probable, therefore, is ultimately owing neither to the one regulation nor to the other, but to that gradual and insensible rise in the real value of silver, which, in the first book of this discourse, I have endeavoured to show, has taken place in the general market of Europe during the course of the present century. It seems to be altogether impossible that the bounty could ever contribute to lower the price of grain.
p4.zh: 据说,自设立这笔赏金以来,玉米的平均价格已大幅下跌。 在上个世纪末,玉米的平均价格开始下跌,并在目前六十四年的头几年里继续下跌,我已经努力表明这一点。 但这件事,假设它是真实的,我相信是的, 一定是在不顾赏金的情况下发生的, 并且不可能是因它而发生的。 在法国和英国都发生过这种情况,尽管在法国不仅没有赏金,而且直到1764年,玉米的出口一直受到普遍禁止。 因此,谷物平均价格的逐步下跌很可能不是由于一项条例,也不是由于另一项条例,而是由于银的实际价值的逐步和不可察觉的上升,在本篇论述的第一册中,我努力表明,在本世纪期间,银的实际价值在欧洲的一般市场中已经出现。赏金似乎完全不可能有助于降低谷物价格。

p5.original: In years of plenty, it has already been observed, the bounty, by occasioning an extraordinary exportation, necessarily keeps up the price of corn in the home market above what it would naturally fall to. To do so was the avowed purpose of the institution. In years of scarcity, though the bounty is frequently suspended, yet the great exportation which it occasions in years of plenty, must frequently hinder, more or less, the plenty of one year from relieving the scarcity of another. Both in years of plenty and in years of scarcity, therefore, the bounty necessarily tends to raise the money price of corn somewhat higher than it otherwise would be in the home market.
p5.zh: 多年来,人们已经注意到,这种特惠性通过引起非同寻常的出口,必然使国内市场上的玉米价格高于其自然会达到的价格。这样做是该机构的公开宗旨。 在资源匮乏的几年中,尽管赏金经常被暂停,但是,在富足的几年中它所出现的巨大出口,必须经常多少地阻碍一年的充足时间来缓解另一年的匮乏。 因此,无论在富裕的年份还是在匮乏的年份,这种赏金都必然会提高玉米的货币价格,比在本土市场上的价格要高一些。

p6.original: That in the actual state of tillage the bounty must necessarily have this tendency, will not, I apprehend, be disputed by any reasonable person. But it has been thought by many people, that it tends to encourage tillage, and that in two different ways; first, by opening a more extensive foreign market to the corn of the farmer, it tends, they imagine, to increase the demand for, and consequently the production of, that commodity; and, secondly by securing to him a better price than he could otherwise expect in the actual state of tillage, it tends, they suppose, to encourage tillage. This double encouragement must they imagine, in a long period of years, occasion such an increase in the production of corn, as may lower its price in the home market, much more than the bounty can raise it in the actual state which tillage may, at the end of that period, happen to be in.
p6.zh: 在实际的耕作状态下,赏金必然有这种倾向,我认为,任何有理智的人都不会对此提出异议。 但许多人认为,它倾向于鼓励耕作,从两种不同的角度来说;第一,通过向农民的玉米开放一个更加广泛的外国市场,他们想象,它倾向于增加对这种商品的需求,从而增加这种商品的生产;第二,通过为他争取比他在耕作实际状态下所预期的更好的价格,他们认为,它倾向于鼓励耕作。 这种双重鼓励必须让他们想象,在很长的几年里,玉米产量会增加,这样可能会降低其在国内市场的价格,比赏金在实际情况下提高的要多得多,在那个时期结束时,种植可能达到的实际状态。

p7.original: I answer, that whatever extension of the foreign market can be occasioned by the bounty must, in every particular year, be altogether at the expense of the home market; as every bushel of corn, which is exported by means of the bounty, and which would not have been exported without the bounty, would have remained in the home market to increase the consumption, and to lower the price of that commodity. The corn bounty, it is to be observed, as well as every other bounty upon exportation, imposes two different taxes upon the people; first, the tax which they are obliged to contribute, in order to pay the bounty; and, secondly, the tax which arises from the advanced price of the commodity in the home market, and which, as the whole body of the people are purchasers of corn, must, in this particular commodity, be paid by the whole body of the people. In this particular commodity, therefore, this second tax is by much the heaviest of the two. Let us suppose that, taking one year with another, the bounty of 5s. upon the exportation of the quarter of wheat raises the price of that commodity in the home market only 6d. the bushel, or 4s. the quarter higher than it otherwise would have been in the actual state of the crop. Even upon this very moderate supposition, the great body of the people, over and above contributing the tax which pays the bounty of 5s. upon every quarter of wheat exported, must pay another of 4s. upon every quarter which they themselves consume. But according to the very well informed author of the Tracts upon the Corn Trade, the average proportion of the corn exported to that consumed at home, is not more than that of one to thirty-one. For every 5s. therefore, which they contribute to the payment of the first tax, they must contribute £6:4s. to the payment of the second. So very heavy a tax upon the first necessary of life-must either reduce the subsistence of the labouring poor, or it must occasion some augmentation in their pecuniary wages, proportionable to that in the pecuniary price of their subsistence. So far as it operates in the one way, it must reduce the ability of the labouring poor to educate and bring up their children, and must, so far, tend to restrain the population of the country. So far as it operate's in the other, it must reduce the ability of the employers of the poor, to employ so great a number as they otherwise might do, and must so far tend to restrain the industry of the country. The extraordinary exportation of corn, therefore occasioned by the bounty, not only in every particular year diminishes the home, just as much as it extends the foreign market and consumption, but, by restraining the population and industry of the country, its final tendency is to stint and restrain the gradual extension of the home market; and thereby, in the long-run, rather to diminish than to augment the whole market and consumption of corn.
p7.zh: 我回答说,无论这种赏金可以给外国市场带来什么延伸,在每一年,都必须完全以牺牲国内市场为代价;因为通过赏金出口的每片玉米,如果没有赏金,本来不会出口的,本来会留在国内市场,以增加消费,降低该商品的价格。玉米的赏金以及出口时的所有其他赏金,对人民征收两种不同的税;第一,为了支付赏金,他们有义务缴纳的税;第二,来自国内市场上商品高级价格的税,由于整个人民是玉米的购买者,因此,在这种特定商品中,必须由全体人民支付。 因此,在这种特定商品中,这种第二税在很大程度上是最重的。 让我们假设,在出口小麦四分之一时,5s的赏金,使该商品在国内市场的价格只提高了6d, 即4s, 高于原作物的实际状况。即使是在这种温和的假设下,除了缴纳5美元赏金的税款外,人民大军还必须缴纳4美元,他们自己消费的每个季度必须缴纳5美元。 但是,根据玉米贸易区非常知情的作者,出口到国内消费的玉米的平均比例不超过一至三十一。 因此,他们每缴纳5英镑,就必须缴纳6:4英镑,缴纳第一笔税款。 因此,对生活所必须的第一需要征收的非常沉重的税,要么减少劳作的穷人的生计,要么必须增加他们的金钱工资,与他们的生计的金钱价格相称。 只要它以一种方式运作,它就必须降低贫困劳动者教育和抚养子女的能力,而且到目前为止,它必须倾向于限制全国的人口。 就经营而言,在另一个方面,它必须降低穷人雇主的能力,雇用他们可能从事的大量工作,并且必须到目前为止限制国家的工业。 因此,由于赏金的缘故,玉米的异乎寻常的出口不仅在每一年都使家产减少,正如它扩大外国市场和消费一样,而且通过限制该国的人口和工业,其最终趋势是抑制和抑制家产市场的逐步扩展;因此,从长远来看,减少而不是扩大整个市场和玉米的消费。

p8.original: This enhancement of the money price of corn, however, it has been thought, by rendering that commodity more profitable to the farmer, must necessarily encourage its production.
p8.zh: 然而,人们认为,通过使玉米对农民更有利可图,提高玉米的货币价格,必然会鼓励其生产。

p9.original: I answer, that this might be the case, if the effect of the bounty was to raise the real price of corn, or to enable the farmer, with an equal quantity of it, to maintain a greater number of labourers in the same manner, whether liberal, moderate, or scanty, than other labourers are commonly maintained in his neighbourhood. But neither the bounty, it is evident, nor any other human institution, can have any such effect. It is not the real, but the nominal price of corn, which can in any considerable degree be affected by the bounty. And though the tax, which that institution imposes upon the whole body of the people, may be very burdensome to those who pay it, it is of very little advantage to those who receive it.
p9.zh: 我回答说,如果赏金的效果是提高玉米的实际价格,或者使数量相等的农民能够以同样的方式维持更多的劳工,无论是自由的,温和的,还是微薄的,都比其他劳工在他所在的附近通常维持的要多. 但显然,这种恩惠或任何其他人类机构都不可能产生任何这种影响。玉米的价格不是真实的,而是名义的,这种价格在相当大程度上会受到赏金的影响。 虽然这个机构给整个人民征收的税,对那些支付税的人来说可能负担很大,但是对于接受税的人来说,它没有什么好处。

p10.original: The real effect of the bounty is not so much to raise the real value of corn, as to degrade the real value of silver; or to make an equal quantity of it exchange for a smaller quantity, not only of corn, but of all other home made commodities; for the money price of corn regulates that of all other home made commodities.
p10.zh: 赏金的实际效果并不在于提高玉米的实际价值,而在于降低银的实际价值;或使同等数量的钱换成数量较少的,不仅玉米,而且所有其他家用商品;因为玉米的金钱价格调节了所有其他家用商品的价格。

p11.original: It regulates the money price of labour, which must always be such as to enable the labourer to purchase a quantity of corn sufficient to maintain him and his family, either in the liberal, moderate, or scanty manner, in which the advancing, stationary, or declining, circumstances of the society, oblige his employers to maintain him.
p11.zh: 它规定劳动力的金钱价格,必须始终使工人能够以自由、温和或微薄的方式购买足以维持他及其家庭的玉米,因为社会的发展、固定或衰落,迫使他的雇主维持他。

p12.original: It regulates the money price of all the other parts of the rude produce of land, which, in every period of improvement, must bear a certain proportion to that of corn, though this proportion is different in different periods. It regulates, for example, the money price of grass and hay, of butcher's meat, of horses, and the maintenance of horses, of land carriage consequently, or of the greater part of the inland commerce of the country.
p12.zh: 它对无礼地生产土地的所有其他部分的货币价格进行调节,这些土地在每一改善期必须具有一定比例的玉米,尽管这个比例在不同时期是不同的. 例如,它规定草和干草、屠夫肉、马、马的维持、陆路运输或国内大部分内陆商业的金钱价格。

p13.original: By regulating the money price of all the other parts of the rude produce of land, it regulates that of the materials of almost all manufactures; by regulating the money price of labour, it regulates that of manufacturing art and industry; and by regulating both, it regulates that of the complete manufacture. The money price of labour, and of every thing that is the produce, either of land or labour, must necessarily either rise or fall in proportion to the money price of corn.
p13.zh: 通过规范无礼土地生产其他部分的物价,规范几乎所有制成品的物价;通过规范劳务的物价,规范制造艺术和工业的物价;通过规范两者,规范整件制成品的物价.劳动力的金钱价格,以及土地或劳动力的每件产品,都必须按照玉米的金钱价格比例上升或下降。

p14.original: Though in consequence of the bounty, therefore, the farmer should be enabled to sell his corn for 4s. the bushel, instead of 3s:6d. and to pay his landlord a money rent proportionable to this rise in the money price of his produce; yet if, in consequence of this rise in the price of corn, 4s. will purchase no more home made goods of any other kind than 3s. 6d. would have done before, neither the circumstances of the farmer, nor those of the landlord, will be much mended by this change. The farmer will not be able to cultivate much better; the landlord will not be able to live much better. In the purchase of foreign commodities, this enhancement in the price of corn may give them some little advantage. In that of home made commodities, it can give them none at all. And almost the whole expense of the farmer, and the far greater part even of that of the landlord, is in home made commodities.
p14.zh: 因此,尽管由于这笔赏金,农民应该能够出售他的玉米,售价为4:6,而不是3:6d。 并向房东支付与其农产品的货币价格上涨相称的租金;然而,如果由于玉米价格上涨,4:4将不再购买3以外的任何家用商品。6d.以前不会这样做,农民的情况和房东的情况都不会因这一变化而大有改观。农民将无法更好地耕种;地主将无法过上更好的生活。 在购买外国商品时,玉米价格的这种提高可能给它们带来一些微小的优势. 在家庭制造商品方面,它完全不会给它们带来任何好处。几乎农民的全部开支,甚至地主的绝大部分开支, 都在家中制造商品。

p15.original: That degradation in the value of silver, which is the effect of the fertility of the mines, and which operates equally, or very nearly equally, through the greater part of the commercial world, is a matter of very little consequence to any particular country. The consequent rise of all money prices, though it does not make those who receive them really richer, does not make them really poorer. A service of plate becomes really cheaper, and every thing else remains precisely of the same real value as before.
p15.zh: 银的贬值是矿山肥力的影响,通过商业界的较大部分,银的产量同样或几乎相等,对任何特定国家的影响很小。随之而来的所有货币价格的上涨,虽然并没有使那些接受货币价格的人真正富裕,但并没有使他们真正贫穷。板块的服务变得非常便宜,其他的每样东西都保持了与以前完全相同的实际价值.

p16.original: But that degradation in the value of silver, which, being the effect either of the peculiar situation or of the political institutions of a particular country, takes place only in that country, is a matter of very great consequence, which, far from tending to make anybody really richer, tends to make every body really poorer. The rise in the money price of all commodities, which is in this case peculiar to that country, tends to discourage more or less every sort of industry which is carried on within it, and to enable foreign nations, by furnishing almost all sorts of goods for a smaller quantity of silver than its own workmen can afford to do, to undersell them, not only in the foreign, but even in the home market.
p16.zh: 但是,银币价值的这种下降,由于某一特定国家的特殊状况或政治体制的影响,只发生在该国,是一个非常大的后果,它远非使任何人真正富裕,而是使每个机构真正贫穷。 所有商品的货币价格的上涨是该国特有的情况,它往往多少会阻止国内从事的每一种行业,并且使外国能够以比本国工人所能负担的更少的白银提供几乎所有种类的商品,从而不仅在外国,甚至在国内市场中,都进行低价出售。

p17.original: It is the peculiar situation of Spain and Portugal, as proprietors of the mines, to be the distributers of gold and silver to all the other countries of Europe. Those metals ought naturally, therefore, to be somewhat cheaper in Spain and Portugal than in any other part of Europe. The difference, however, should be no more than the amount of the freight and insurance; and, on account of the great value and small bulk of those metals, their freight is no great matter, and their insurance is the same as that of any other goods of equal value. Spain and Portugal, therefore, could suffer very little from their peculiar situation, if they did not aggravate its disadvantages by their political institutions.
p17.zh: 西班牙和葡萄牙作为矿山的所有人,作为黄金和白银向欧洲所有其他国家分发是其特殊情况。 因此,在西班牙和葡萄牙,这些金属自然比欧洲任何其他地区要便宜一些。 然而,其差别不应大于运费和保险金额;而且,由于这些金属的价值巨大,且其数量很少,因此其运费并不大,其保险额与任何其他同等价值的货物相同。 因此,如果西班牙和葡萄牙不因政治机构而加剧其不利处境,那么它们不会因自己的特殊处境而受多大的伤害。

p18.original: Spain by taxing, and Portugal by prohibiting, the exportation of gold and silver, load that exportation with the expense of smuggling, and raise the value of those metals in other countries so much more above what it is in their own, by the whole amount of this expense. When you dam up a stream of water, as soon as the dam is full, as much water must run over the dam-head as if there was no dam at all. The prohibition of exportation cannot detain a greater quantity of gold and silver in Spain and Portugal, than what they can afford to employ, than what the annual produce of their land and labour will allow them to employ, in coin, plate, gilding, and other ornaments of gold and silver. When they have got this quantity, the dam is full, and the whole stream which flows in afterwards must run over. The annual exportation of gold and silver from Spain and Portugal, accordingly, is, by all accounts, notwithstanding these restraints, very near equal to the whole annual importation. As the water, however, must always be deeper behind the dam-head than before it, so the quantity of gold and silver which these restraints detain in Spain and Portugal, must, in proportion to the annual produce of their land and labour, be greater than what is to be found in other countries. The higher and stronger the dam-head, the greater must be the difference in the depth of water behind and before it. The higher the tax, the higher the penalties with which the prohibition is guarded, the more vigilant and severe the police which looks after the execution of the law, the greater must be the difference in the proportion of gold and silver to the annual produce of the land and labour of Spain and Portugal, and to that of other countries. It is said, accordingly, to be very considerable, and that you frequently find there a profusion of plate in houses, where there is nothing else which would in other countries be thought suitable or correspondent to this sort of magnificence. The cheapness of gold and silver, or, what is the same thing, the dearness of all commodities, which is the necessary effect of this redundancy of the precious metals, discourages both the agriculture and manufactures of Spain and Portugal, and enables foreign nations to supply them with many sorts of rude, and with almost all sorts of manufactured produce, for a smaller quantity of gold and silver than what they themselves can either raise or make them for at home. The tax and prohibition operate in two different ways. They not only lower very much the value of the precious metals in Spain and Portugal, but by detaining there a certain quantity of those metals which would otherwise flow over other countries, they keep up their value in those other countries somewhat above what it otherwise would be, and thereby give those countries a double advantage in their commerce with Spain and Portugal. Open the flood-gates, and there will presently be less water above, and more below the dam-head, and it will soon come to a level in both places. Remove the tax and the prohibition, and as the quantity of gold and silver will diminish considerably in Spain and Portugal, so it will increase somewhat in other countries; and the value of those metals, their proportion to the annual produce of land and labour, will soon come to a level, or very near to a level, in all. The loss which Spain and Portugal could sustain by this exportation of their gold and silver, would be altogether nominal and imaginary. The nominal value of their goods, and of the annual produce of their land and labour, would fall, and would be expressed or represented by a smaller quantity of silver than before; but their real value would be the same as before, and would be sufficient to maintain, command, and employ the same quantity of labour. As the nominal value of their goods would fall, the real value of what remained of their gold and silver would rise, and a smaller quantity of those metals would answer all the same purposes of commerce and circulation which had employed a greater quantity before. The gold and silver which would go abroad would not go abroad for nothing, but would bring back an equal value of goods of some kind or other. Those goods, too, would not be all matters of mere luxury and expense, to be consumed by idle people, who produce nothing in return for their consumption. As the real wealth and revenue of idle people would not be augmented by this extraordinary exportation of gold and silver, so neither would their consumption be much augmented by it. Those goods would probably, the greater part of them, and certainly some part of them, consist in materials, tools, and provisions, for the employment and maintenance of industrious people, who would reproduce, with a profit, the full value of their consumption. A part of the dead stock of the society would thus be turned into active stock, and would put into motion a greater quantity of industry than had been employed before. The annual produce of their land and labour would immediately be augmented a little, and in a few years would probably be augmented a great deal; their industry being thus relieved from one of the most oppressive burdens which it at present labours under.
p18.zh: 西班牙对黄金和白银出口征税,葡萄牙对黄金和白银出口加以禁止,以走私为代价,并在其他国家将这些金属的价值提高得远远高于其本身的价值,而这一费用则超过其全部数额。坝子一满,就把水堵上河水, 坝头上必须挤满多少水, 好像根本没有大坝一样。 在西班牙和葡萄牙,禁止出口的金银数量不能超过它们能够雇用的金银数量,而不能超过它们每年的土地和劳力产量允许它们使用硬币、板子、金银和其他金银饰品的数量。 当他们得到这个数量时,大坝是满的, 整个流进之后的溪流必须碾过。 因此,尽管存在这些限制,西班牙和葡萄牙每年出口的黄金和白银与全年进口几乎相等。 然而,由于水必须始终比以前更深地位于坝头后面,因此,这些限制在西班牙和葡萄牙所扣留的金银数量必须比在其他国家所发现的要多,与其土地和劳动力的年产量成比例。坝头越高越强,其后及前方水深的差别必然越大.税收越高,守法处罚越严厉,执法后看守的警察越警惕,越严厉,金银在西班牙和葡萄牙的土地和劳动力年产量中的比例差异越大,与其他国家的差别也就越大. 因此,人们说,这相当可观,而且你经常发现,房屋里有一大堆盘子,在别的国家,没有任何东西可以被认为适合或与这种放大相呼应。 金银的便宜,或者说,同物,所有商品的贫乏,这是这种贵金属冗余的必要效果,使西班牙和葡萄牙的农业和制造业都望而却步,使外国能够以多种粗鲁,几乎各种制成品,供应数量比他们自己可以自己提炼或制造的要少的金银.征税和禁止以两种不同的方式运作。 它们不仅大大降低了西班牙和葡萄牙贵金属的价值,而且把本来会流过其他国家的一定数量的贵金属扣留在那里,保持了在这些国家的价值,略高于原来的价值,从而使这些国家在与西班牙和葡萄牙的商务中享有双重优势。开洪闸,目前上下水少,下坝头多,两处水位很快达到水位.取消税收和禁令,随着西班牙和葡萄牙的金银数量将大幅下降,其他国家将有所增长;这些金属的价值及其在土地和劳动力年产量中的比例将很快达到某种水平,或接近某一水平。 西班牙和葡萄牙因黄金和白银出口而承受的损失完全是名义上的和想象的。其货面值,以及其土地和劳力年产值,将下降,以比以前少的银元表示或表示;但其实际价值与以前相同,足以维持,指挥,使用同样数量的劳力. 随着其商品的名义价值下降,其金银的实际价值将上升,这些金属中数量较少的金属将满足以前使用数量较多的相同商业和流通目的。将出国的金银不会白白地出国,而是会带回某种或其他商品的同等价值。 这些商品也不仅仅是奢侈品和费用问题,而是被闲置的人消费,他们不生产任何产品来换取他们的消费。 由于这种非同寻常的黄金和白银出口不会增加闲民的实际财富和收入,因此他们的消费也不会因此而大大增加。 这些商品可能包括材料、工具和规定,用于雇用和维持勤劳的人,他们可以以利润来创造其消费的全部价值。 因此,社会中一部分已死库存将变成活跃库存,并将比以前更多地投入工业。 他们的土地和劳动力的年产量将立即增加一点,在几年内很可能增加很多;因此,他们的工业摆脱了目前它所承受的最压迫性负担之一。

p19.original: The bounty upon the exportation of corn necessarily operates exactly in the same way as this absurd policy of Spain and Portugal. Whatever be the actual state of tillage, it renders our corn somewhat dearer in the home market than it otherwise would be in that state, and somewhat cheaper in the foreign; and as the average money price of corn regulates, more or less, that of all other commodities, it lowers the value of silver considerably in the one, and tends to raise it a little in the other. It enables foreigners, the Dutch in particular, not only to eat our corn cheaper than they otherwise could do, but sometimes to eat it cheaper than even our own people can do upon the same occasions; as we are assured by an excellent authority, that of Sir Matthew Decker. It hinders our own workmen from furnishing their goods for so small a quantity of silver as they otherwise might do, and enables the Dutch to furnish theirs for a smaller. It tends to render our manufactures somewhat dearer in every market, and theirs somewhat cheaper, than they otherwise would be, and consequently to give their industry a double advantage over our own.
p19.zh: 对玉米出口的奖励必然与西班牙和葡萄牙的这种荒谬政策完全相同。 无论耕作的实际状况如何,它使我们的玉米在家庭市场比在其他市场更珍贵,在外国也更便宜;随着玉米的平均货币价格多少能调节所有其他商品的价格,它大大降低了银的价值,并倾向于在另一商品中略微提高。 它使外国人,特别是荷兰人,不仅能够比他们本来可以做的便宜地吃我们的玉米,而且有时甚至比我们本国人民在同样场合能够做的便宜;正如我们得到一个出色的权威——马修·德克尔爵士的权威——保证的那样。 它阻碍我们自己的工人为自己的货物提供数量如此之少的白银,并使得荷兰人能够为更少的白银提供货物。 它往往使我们的制成品在每一个市场都更加珍贵,它们的制成品比它们便宜一些,从而使它们的工业比我们自己的工业拥有双重优势。

p20.original: The bounty, as it raises in the home market, not so much the real, as the nominal price of our corn; as it augments, not the quantity of labour which a certain quantity of corn can maintain and employ, but only the quantity of silver which it will exchange for; it discourages our manufactures, without rendering any considerable service, either to our farmers or country gentlemen. It puts, indeed, a little more money into the pockets of both, and it will perhaps be somewhat difficult to persuade the greater part of them that this is not rendering them a very considerable service. But if this money sinks in its value, in the quantity of labour, provisions, and home-made commodities of all different kinds which it is capable of purchasing, as much as it rises in its quantity, the service will be little more than nominal and imaginary.
p20.zh: 这笔赏金在家庭市场上增加,而不是真正的,而是我们玉米的名义价格;它增加的不是一定数量的玉米能够维持和雇用的劳动力数量,而是它所要交换的银子数量;它使我们的制造业受到挫折,而不会为我们农民或乡绅提供任何可观的服务。 事实上,这给两者的口袋都增加了一点资金,也许很难说服他们中的多数人,认为这不会使他们获得相当可观的服务。 但是,如果这种货币在价值、劳动力数量、供应量和能够购买的各种自制商品方面,随着数量的增长,其服务将小于名义和想象。

p21.original: There is, perhaps, but one set of men in the whole commonwealth to whom the bounty either was or could be essentially serviceable. These were the corn merchants, the exporters and importers of corn. In years of plenty, the bounty necessarily occasioned a greater exportation than would otherwise have taken place; and by hindering the plenty of the one year from relieving the scarcity of another, it occasioned in years of scarcity a greater importation than would otherwise have been necessary. It increased the business of the corn merchant in both; and in the years of scarcity, it not only enabled him to import a greater quantity, but to sell it for a better price, and consequently with a greater profit, than he could otherwise have made, if the plenty of one year had not been more or less hindered from relieving the scarcity of another. It is in this set of men, accordingly, that I have observed the greatest zeal for the continuance or renewal of the bounty.
p21.zh: 也许是,但整个联邦中有一队人 赏金要么是给的,要么是可以用的 这些是玉米商、玉米进出口商。 在富饶的岁月中,这种赏金必然导致出口量超过本来会出口的数量;通过阻止一年中大量出口量缓解另一年的稀缺量,在缺乏的岁月中,这种收入比本来需要的进口量要大。 它增加了玉米商在这两个方面的业务;在短缺的岁月里,它不仅使他能够进口更多的粮食,而且能够以更好的价格出售粮食,因此,如果一年的粮食没有多少地妨碍减少另一个粮食短缺,则其利润会比他本来可以赚得的多。 因此,正是在这些人中,我对继续或延长赏金表现出了最大的热情。

p22.original: Our country gentlemen, when they imposed the high duties upon the exportation of foreign corn, which in times of moderate plenty amount to a prohibition, and when they established the bounty, seem to have imitated the conduct of our manufacturers. By the one institution, they secured to themselves the monopoly of the home market, and by the other they endeavoured to prevent that market from ever being overstocked with their commodity. By both they endeavoured to raise its real value, in the same manner as our manufacturers had, by the like institutions, raised the real value of many different sorts of manufactured goods. They did not, perhaps, attend to the great and essential difference which nature has established between corn and almost every other sort of goods. When, either by the monopoly of the home market, or by a bounty upon exportation, you enable our woollen or linen manufacturers to sell their goods for somewhat a better price than they otherwise could get for them, you raise, not only the nominal, but the real price of those goods; you render them equivalent to a greater quantity of labour and subsistence; you increase not only the nominal, but the real profit, the real wealth and revenue of those manufacturers; and you enable them, either to live better themselves, or to employ a greater quantity of labour in those particular manufactures. You really encourage those manufactures, and direct towards them a greater quantity of the industry of the country than what would properly go to them of its own accord. But when, by the like institutions, you raise the nominal or money price of corn, you do not raise its real value; you do not increase the real wealth, the real revenue, either of our farmers or country gentlemen; you do not encourage the growth of corn, because you do not enable them to maintain and employ more labourers in raising it. The nature of things has stamped upon corn a real value, which cannot be altered by merely altering its money price. No bounty upon exportation, no monopoly of the home market, can raise that value. The freest competition cannot lower it, Through the world in general, that value is equal to the quantity of labour which it can maintain, and in every particular place it is equal to the quantity of labour which it can maintain in the way, whether liberal, moderate, or scanty, in which labour is commonly maintained in that place. Woollen or linen cloth are not the regulating commodities by which the real value of all other commodities must be finally measured and determined; corn is. The real value of every other commodity is finally measured and determined by the proportion which its average money price bears to the average money price of corn. The real value of corn does not vary with those variations in its average money price, which sometimes occur from one century to another; it is the real value of silver which varies with them.
p22.zh: 我国的先生们,当他们对出口外国玉米征收高额关税时,在数量适中的情况下,这种关税相当于禁止,当他们确定赏金时,似乎模仿了我们制造商的行为。由一个机构,它们为自己垄断了国内市场,另一个机构则努力防止该市场被其商品过度囤积。 他们都努力提高它的实际价值,就像我们的制造商通过类似机构提高了许多不同种类的制成品的实际价值一样。 他们也许没有注意大自然在玉米和几乎所有其他种类商品之间建立的巨大和根本的区别。无论是通过对国内市场的垄断,还是通过出口时的赏金,你使我们的羊绒或亚麻制造商能够以比他们本来可以得到的好一些的价格出售他们的商品,你不仅提高这些商品的名义价格,而且提高这些商品的实际价格;你使这些商品相当于更多的劳力和生计;你不仅增加这些制造商的名义利润,而且增加它们的实际利润、实际财富和收入;你使他们能够更好地生活,或在这些特定制造业中雇用更多的劳力。 你们真的鼓励这些制造品, 并且把更多的国家工业 提供给他们, 而不是它们自己会得到的。 但是,当通过类似的机构,提高玉米的名义价格或货币价格时,你不会提高它的实际价值;你不会增加真正的财富,真正的收入,无论是我们的农民还是乡绅;你不会鼓励玉米的种植,因为你无法让他们维持和雇用更多的劳工来种植玉米。玉米本身就具有真实价值,不能仅仅通过改变其货币价格来改变这种价值。任何对出口的赏金,任何对国内市场的垄断,都不能提高这一价值。 最自由的竞争不能通过整个世界来降低这一价值,它等于它能够维持的劳动力数量,在每一个特定的地方,它都等于它能够维持的劳动力数量,无论是自由的、温和的还是微薄的,在那里通常维持着劳动力。伍伦布或亚麻布并不是最终衡量和确定所有其他商品实际价值的调节商品;玉米就是如此。最终衡量和确定所有其他商品的实际价值,是根据其平均货币价格与玉米平均货币价格的比例。玉米的实际价值与其平均货币价格的这些变化并不不同,有时这种变化发生在一个世纪之间;而银的实际价值则随它们而不同。

p23.original: Bounties upon the exportation of any homemade commodity are liable, first, to that general objection which may be made to all the different expedients of the mercantile system; the objection of forcing some part of the industry of the country into a channel less advantageous than that in which it would run of its own accord; and, secondly, to the particular objection of forcing it not only into a channel that is less advantageous, but into one that is actually disadvantageous; the trade which cannot be carried on but by means of a bounty being necessarily a losing trade. The bounty upon the exportation of corn is liable to this further objection, that it can in no respect promote the raising of that particular commodity of which it was meant to encourage the production. When our country gentlemen, therefore, demanded the establishment of the bounty, though they acted in imitation of our merchants and manufacturers, they did not act with that complete comprehension of their own interest, which commonly directs the conduct of those two other orders of people. They loaded the public revenue with a very considerable expense: they imposed a very heavy tax upon the whole body of the people; but they did not, in any sensible degree, increase the real value of their own commodity; and by lowering somewhat the real value of silver, they discouraged, in some degree, the general industry of the country, and, instead of advancing, retarded more or less the improvement of their own lands, which necessarily depend upon the general industry of the country.
p23.zh: 出口任何自制商品的利润首先要对下述情况负责:对商业系统的所有不同方便可能提出的普遍反对;反对强迫该国部分产业进入比它自己经营的渠道更不利的渠道;第二,特别反对强迫它进入一个不仅不那么有利的渠道,而且实际上处于不利地位的渠道;不能进行贸易,但通过赏金进行的贸易必然是一种亏损的贸易。出口玉米的赏金会引起这种进一步的反对,即它绝对不能促进种植它本来要鼓励生产的这种特定商品。 因此,当我国的先生们要求建立赏金时,尽管他们模仿我们的商家和制造商,但他们并没有完全理解他们自己的利益,这通常指导着另外两种人的行为。 他们把公共收入加满了相当可观的开支:他们对整个人民征收了非常沉重的税;但是他们并没有在任何合理程度上增加他们自己的商品的实际价值;通过在某种程度上降低银的实际价值,他们在一定程度上劝阻了国家的一般工业,而不是推进或多或少地阻碍他们自己土地的改良,而这种改良必然依赖于国家的一般工业。

p24.original: To encourage the production of any commodity, a bounty upon production, one should imagine, would have a more direct operation than one upon exportation. It would, besides, impose only one tax upon the people, that which they must contribute in order to pay the bounty. Instead of raising, it would tend to lower the price of the commodity in the home market; and thereby, instead of imposing a second tax upon the people, it might, at least in part, repay them for what they had contributed to the first. Bounties upon production, however, have been very rarely granted. The prejudices established by the commercial system have taught us to believe, that national wealth arises more immediately from exportation than from production. It has been more favoured, accordingly, as the more immediate means of bringing money into the country. Bounties upon production, it has been said too, have been found by experience more liable to frauds than those upon exportation. How far this is true, I know not. That bounties upon exportation have been abused, to many fraudulent purposes, is very well known. But it is not the interest of merchants and manufacturers, the great inventors of all these expedients, that the home market should be overstocked with their goods; an event which a bounty upon production might sometimes occasion. A bounty upon exportation, by enabling them to send abroad their surplus part, and to keep up the price of what remains in the home market, effectually prevents this. Of all the expedients of the mercantile system, accordingly, it is the one of which they are the fondest. I have known the different undertakers of some particular works agree privately among themselves to give a bounty out of their own pockets upon the exportation of a certain proportion of the goods which they dealt in. This expedient succeeded so well, that it more than doubled the price of their goods in the home market, notwithstanding a very considerable increase in the produce. The operation of the bounty upon corn must have been wonderfully different, if it has lowered the money price of that commodity.
p24.zh: 为了鼓励任何商品的生产,应该设想,在生产时的赏金比出口时的赏金更直接。 此外,它只给人民征收一种税,他们必须缴纳一笔税,才能支付赏金。 它不会提高,而是倾向于降低商品在母国市场的价格;因此,它不会对人民征收第二税,而至少部分地可能补偿他们对第一税的贡献。 然而,很少给予生产上的好处。商业制度所形成的偏见使我们相信,国家财富更直接来自出口,而不是生产。 因此,人们更倾向于把它作为将资金带入该国的更直接的手段。 据说,经验也发现,生产时的丰厚价值比出口时的丰厚价值更可能发生欺诈。 这有多远,我不知道。出口收益被滥用到许多欺诈目的,这是众所周知的。 但是,这些权宜之计的伟大发明者 -- -- 商人和制造商 -- -- 的利益并不在于家用市场应过度储存他们的商品;有时在生产时可能出现这种特惠事件。出口的赏金,使它们能够将剩余部分运出国外,并保持国内市场剩余部分的价格,实际上阻止了出口。 在商贸系统的所有权宜之计中,它因此是最受欢迎的。 我知道,某些特定作品的不同承业者私下同意,在出口他们交易的某一部分货物时,从他们自己的口袋中提供一笔赏金。 这一权宜之计取得了如此成功,尽管农产品大幅增长,但其在国内市场上的商品价格却翻了一番多。玉米的赏金的操作如果降低了这种商品的货币价格,肯定大不相同。

p25.original: Something like a bounty upon production, however, has been granted upon some particular occasions. The tonnage bounties given to the white herring and whale fisheries may, perhaps, be considered as somewhat of this nature. They tend directly, it may be supposed, to render the goods cheaper in the home market than they otherwise would be. In other respects, their effects, it must be acknowledged, are the same as those of bounties upon exportation. By means of them, a part of the capital of the country is employed in bringing goods to market, of which the price does not repay the cost, together with the ordinary profits of stock.
p25.zh: 然而,在某些特定场合,已经给予一些像生产奖励的东西。给予白鹭和鲸鱼捕捞的吨位丰厚也许可以被认为是某种性质的。 它们往往直接,也许应该使商品在国内市场上比其他商品便宜。 在其他方面,必须承认,其效果与出口时的效益相同。 通过它们,国家一部分资本被用于将商品带入市场,其中价格不偿还成本,加上股票的普通利润.

p26.original: But though the tonnage bounties to those fisheries do not contribute to the opulence of the nation, it may, perhaps, be thought that they contribute to its defence, by augmenting the number of its sailors and shipping. This, it may be alleged, may sometimes be done by means of such bounties, at a much smaller expense than by keeping up a great standing navy, if I may use such an expression, in the same way as a standing army.
p26.zh: 但是,虽然这些渔业的吨位丰厚无助于国家的繁荣,但也许可以认为,它们通过增加其水手和航运的数量,为国防作出了贡献。可以说,这有时可能通过这种丰厚的手段来实现,其费用远低于维持一支伟大的海军,如果我可以象常备部队那样使用这种表达方式。

p27.original: Notwithstanding these favourable allegations, however, the following considerations dispose me to believe, that in granting at least one of these bounties, the legislature has been very grossly imposed upon:
p27.zh: 然而,尽管有这些有利的指控,但以下考虑使我不得不相信,在给予其中至少一项好处时,立法机构被严重强加给:

p28.original: First, The herring-buss bounty seems too large.
p28.zh: 首先 牧民的赏金似乎太大了

p29.original: From the commencement of the winter fishing 1771, to the end of the winter fishing 1781, the tonnage bounty upon the herring-buss fishery has been at thirty shillings the ton. During these eleven years, the whole number of barrels caught by the herring-buss fishery of Scotland amounted to 378,347. The herrings caught and cured at sea are called sea-sticks. In order to render them what are called merchantable herrings, it is necessary to repack them with an additional quantity of salt; and in this case, it is reckoned, that three barrels of sea-sticks are usually repacked into two barrels of merchantable herrings. The number of barrels of merchantable herrings, therefore, caught during these eleven years, will amount only, according to this account, to 252,231¼. During these eleven years, the tonnage bounties paid amounted to £155,463:11s. or 8s:2¼d. upon every barrel of sea-sticks, and to 12s:3¾d. upon every barrel of merchantable herrings.
p29.zh: 从1771年冬季捕鱼开始,到1781年冬季捕鱼结束,牧民巴士渔业的吨位赏金一直为30先令吨. 在这11年中,苏格兰的蟑螂-公共汽车渔业捕获的桶数达378 347桶。 在海上捕捉并治愈的 ⁇ 鱼称为"海 ⁇ ". 为了让它们成为所谓的可买卖的 ⁇ 鱼,必须重新包装,增加盐量;在这种情况下,可以估计,三桶海棍通常被重新包装成两桶可买卖的 ⁇ 鱼. 因此,根据这一说法,在这11年中捕获的可出售的驯鹿的桶数量将仅为252 2311⁄4。 在这11年中,每桶海棍的吨位丰收额为155 463:11英镑或8:21⁄4d,每桶可买卖的 ⁇ 鱼的吨位丰收额为12:33⁄4d。

p30.original: The salt with which these herrings are cured is sometimes Scotch, and sometimes foreign salt; both which are delivered, free of all excise duty, to the fish-curers. The excise duty upon Scotch salt is at present 1s:6d., that upon foreign salt 10s. the bushel. A barrel of herrings is supposed to require about one bushel and one-fourth of a bushel foreign salt. Two bushels are the supposed average of Scotch salt. If the herrings are entered for exportation, no part of this duty is paid up; if entered for home consumption, whether the herrings were cured with foreign or with Scotch salt, only one shilling the barrel is paid up. It was the old Scotch duty upon a bushel of salt, the quantity which, at a low estimation, had been supposed necessary for curing a barrel of herrings. In Scotland, foreign salt is very little used for any other purpose but the curing of fish. But from the 5th April 1771 to the 5th April 1782, the quantity of foreign salt imported amounted to 936,974 bushels, at eighty-four pounds the bushel; the quantity of Scotch salt delivered from the works to the fish-curers, to no more than 168,226, at fifty-six pounds the bushel only. It would appear, therefore, that it is principally foreign salt that is used in the fisheries. Upon every barrel of herrings exported, there is, besides, a bounty of 2s:8d. and more than two-thirds of the buss-caught herrings are exported. Put all these things together, and you will find that, during these eleven years, every barrel of buss-caught herrings, cured with Scotch salt, when exported, has cost government 17s:11¾d.; and, when entered for home consumption, 14s:3¾d.; and that every barrel cured with foreign salt, when exported, has cost government £1:7:5¾d.; and, when entered for home consumption, £1:3:9¾d. The price of a barrel of good merchantable herrings runs from seventeen and eighteen to four and five-and-twenty shillings; about a guinea at an average. {See the accounts at the end of this Book.}
p30.zh: 用来治愈这些 ⁇ 的盐有时是苏格兰盐,有时是外国盐;这两种盐都免费交付给鱼 ⁇ 者。威士忌盐的消费税目前为1:6d,即10s的外国盐。 一桶 ⁇ 草原需约一株灌木和四分之一的灌木外国盐.两种灌木是苏格兰盐的平均值 如果为出口而输入了 ⁇ 鱼,则不支付该义务的任何部分;如果为家庭消费而输入,无论 ⁇ 鱼是用外国盐还是苏格兰盐治愈的,只支付一先令桶。这是一种旧的威士忌税,对一整桶盐来说,这种盐的数量在低估上被认为是治疗一桶 ⁇ 鱼所必需的。 在苏格兰,除治鱼外,外国盐很少用于任何其他目的。 但从1771年4月5日到1782年4月5日,进口的外国盐数量达936,974灌木,灌木为84磅;从作品中送给鱼 ⁇ 的苏格兰盐数量不超过168,226磅,只有灌木为56磅. 因此,渔业中使用的主要是外国盐。 此外,每出口一桶 ⁇ ,就有2:8d的赏金,三分之二以上的公交车抓获的 ⁇ 被出口。把这些东西放在一起,你会发现,在这11年里,每桶公交车抓获的 ⁇ ,用苏格兰盐治愈,出口时,政府花费17:113⁄4d;输入家用时,14:33⁄4d;每桶用外国盐治愈,出口时政府花费1:7:53⁄4d;输入家用时,1:3:93⁄4d. 一桶可买卖的好生草药的价格从17先令和18先令到4先令和5先令和20先令不等;平均大约是1先令。 {参见本书结尾的账目。 }

p31.original: Secondly, The bounty to the white-herring fishery is a tonnage bounty, and is proportioned to the burden of the ship, not to her diligence or success in the fishery; and it has, I am afraid, been too common for the vessels to fit out for the sole purpose of catching, not the fish but the bounty. In the year 1759, when the bounty was at fifty shillings the ton, the whole buss fishery of Scotland brought in only four barrels of sea-sticks. In that year, each barrel of sea-sticks cost government, in bounties alone, £113:15s.; each barrel of merchantable herrings £159:7:6.
p31.zh: 第二,对白鲸渔业的赏金是一种吨位赏金,与船舶的负担成比例,而不是与她在渔业中的勤奋或成功相称;恐怕,这太常见了,使这些渔船无法适应捕捞的唯一目的,而不是鱼,而是与赏金相称。 在1759年,当赏金是50先令时, 吨, 整个公交车渔业 苏格兰只带来了四桶的海棍。 在那一年,每桶海棍花费政府,光是丰收,就113:15英镑;每桶可买卖的 ⁇ 鱼就花费159:7:6.

p32.original: Thirdly, The mode of fishing, for which this tonnage bounty in the white herring fishery has been given (by busses or decked vessels from twenty to eighty tons burden ), seems not so well adapted to the situation of Scotland, as to that of Holland, from the practice of which country it appears to have been borrowed. Holland lies at a great distance from the seas to which herrings are known principally to resort, and can, therefore, carry on that fishery only in decked vessels, which can carry water and provisions sufficient for a voyage to a distant sea; but the Hebrides, or Western Islands, the islands of Shetland, and the northern and north-western coasts of Scotland, the countries in whose neighbourhood the herring fishery is principally carried on, are everywhere intersected by arms of the sea, which run up a considerable way into the land, and which, in the language of the country, are called sea-lochs. It is to these sea-lochs that the herrings principally resort during the seasons in which they visit these seas; for the visits of this, and, I am assured, of many other sorts of fish, are not quite regular and constant. A boat-fishery, therefore, seems to be the mode of fishing best adapted to the peculiar situation of Scotland, the fishers carrying the herrings on shore as fast as they are taken, to be either cured or consumed fresh. But the great encouragement which a bounty of 30s. the ton gives to the buss-fishery, is necessarily a discouragement to the boat-fishery, which, having no such bounty, cannot bring its cured fish to market upon the same terms as the buss-fishery. The boat-fishery; accordingly, which, before the establishment of the buss-bounty, was very considerable, and is said to have employed a number of seamen, not inferior to what the buss-fishery employs at present, is now gone almost entirely to decay. Of the former extent, however, of this now ruined and abandoned fishery, I must acknowledge that I cannot pretend to speak with much precision. As no bounty was-paid upon the outfit of the boat-fishery, no account was taken of it by the officers of the customs or salt duties.
p32.zh: 第三,在白鹭渔场上给予这种吨位赏金的捕鱼方式(通过20吨至80吨的巴士或甲板船),似乎与荷兰的情况相比,似乎不太适合苏格兰的情况,而荷兰的做法似乎是借用了它。 荷兰位于离众所周知主要使用牧民的海域很远的地方,因此只能靠甲板船进行捕捞,这些船可以运载水和足够航行到远海的补给;但赫布里底群岛,或西群岛,谢特兰群岛,以及苏格兰北部和西北部海岸,其邻近地区主要从事牧民渔业的国家,到处是海上武器交汇之处,这些武器大量流入陆地,用该国的语言称为 " 海螺 " 。牧民们主要在考察这些海洋的季节里,在这些海洋中游览;对于这种游览,而且我确信,许多其他种类的鱼类,他们并不经常和经常地游览。 因此,渔船捕鱼似乎是最适合苏格兰特殊情况的捕鱼方式,渔民在岸上携带的鲱鱼速度快一些,要么被治愈,要么被新鲜消费。 但是,30多吨的赏金给予大巴钓鱼业的巨大鼓励,必然是对大巴钓鱼业的劝阻,因为大巴钓鱼业没有这种赏金,不能以大巴钓鱼业的同样条件将它治好的鱼上市. 因此,在公交车设立之前,该船的捕鱼业相当庞大,据说雇用了一些海员,不低于目前该船的捕鱼业,现在几乎已完全衰败。 然而,就以前的情况而言,现在这种被破坏和遗弃的渔业,我必须承认,我不能假装非常精确地发言。 由于没有向渔船捕鱼队的服装支付赏金,海关或盐税官员没有考虑到这一点。

p33.original: Fourthly, In many parts of Scotland, during certain seasons of the year, herrings make no inconsiderable part of the food of the common people. A bounty which tended to lower their price in the home market, might contribute a good deal to the relief of a great number of our fellow-subjects, whose circumstances are by no means affluent. But the herring-bus bounty contributes to no such good purpose. It has ruined the boat fishery, which is by far the best adapted for the supply of the home market; and the additional bounty of 2s:8d. the barrel upon exportation, carries the greater part, more than two-thirds, of the produce of the buss-fishery abroad. Between thirty and forty years ago, before the establishment of the buss-bounty, 16s. the barrel, I have been assured, was the common price of white herrings. Between ten and fifteen years ago, before the boat-fishery was entirely ruined, the price was said to have run from seventeen to twenty shillings the barrel. For these last five years, it has, at an average, been at twenty-five shillings the barrel. This high price, however, may have been owing to the real scarcity of the herrings upon the coast of Scotland. I must observe, too, that the cask or barrel, which is usually sold with the herrings, and of which the price is included in all the foregoing prices, has, since the commencement of the American war, risen to about double its former price, or from about 3s. to about 6s. I must likewise observe, that the accounts I have received of the prices of former times, have been by no means quite uniform and consistent, and an old man of great accuracy and experience has assured me, that, more than fifty years ago, a guinea was the usual price of a barrel of good merchantable herrings; and this, I imagine, may still be looked upon as the average price. All accounts, however, I think, agree that the price has not been lowered in the home market in consequence of the buss-bounty.
p33.zh: 第四,在苏格兰的许多地方,在一年中的某些季节里,牧民不会成为普通人的食物中不小的一部分。一种往往降低其在国内市场价格的赏金,可能大大有助于拯救我们许多同伴,他们的情况绝不是富裕的。 但是,牧民巴士的赏金 却无济于事 它摧毁了远为最适于国内市场供应的渔船渔业;出口时的桶子额外收入为2:8d,其中三分之二以上是国外公共汽车渔业产品。 三四十年前,公交车成立前,16s. 枪管,我已保证,是白鹭的常见价格.10到15年前,在船钓船厂被彻底摧毁之前,据说价格从17先令到20先令不等。 这五年来,桶平均为25先令。 然而,这种高昂的价格可能是由于苏格兰海岸的牧民真正稀缺。 我还必须看到,通常与牧民一起出售的桶或桶,其价格包含在上述所有价格中,自美国战争开始以来,已经上升到了原来的价格的大约两倍,或者从大约3s上升到大约6s。 同样,我必须指出,我收到的关于以前价格的叙述绝非十分统一和一致,而且一位非常准确和经验丰富的老人向我保证,50多年前,一桶可买卖的好驯鹿的通常价格是豚鼠;我想,这仍可视为平均价格。 然而,我认为,所有说法都同意,由于公共汽车的行驶,国内市场的价格并没有降低。

p34.original: When the undertakers of fisheries, after such liberal bounties have been bestowed upon them, continue to sell their commodity at the same, or even at a higher price than they were accustomed to do before, it might be expected that their profits should be very great; and it is not improbable that those of some individuals may have been so. In general, however, I have every reason to believe they have been quite otherwise. The usual effect of such bounties is, to encourage rash undertakers to adventure in a business which they do not understand; and what they lose by their own negligence and ignorance, more than compensates all that they can gain by the utmost liberality of government. In 1750, by the same act which first gave the bounty of 30s. the ton for the encouragement of the white herring fishery (the 23d Geo. II. chap. 24), a joint stock company was erected, with a capital of £500,000, to which the subscribers (over and above all other encouragements, the tonnage bounty just now mentioned, the exportation bounty of 2s:8d. the barrel, the delivery of both British and foreign salt duty free) were, during the space of fourteen years, for every hundred pounds which they subscribed and paid into the stock of the society, entitled to three pounds a-year, to be paid by the receiver-general of the customs in equal half-yearly payments. Besides this great company, the residence of whose governor and directors was to be in London, it was declared lawful to erect different fishing chambers in all the different out-ports of the kingdom, provided a sum not less than £10,000 was subscribed into the capital of each, to be managed at its own risk, and for its own profit and loss. The same annuity, and the same encouragements of all kinds, were given to the trade of those inferior chambers as to that of the great company. The subscription of the great company was soon filled up, and several different fishing chambers were erected in the different out-ports of the kingdom. In spite of all these encouragements, almost all those different companies, both great and small, lost either the whole or the greater part of their capitals; scarce a vestige now remains of any of them, and the white-herring fishery is now entirely, or almost entirely, carried on by private adventurers.
p34.zh: 当渔业的经营者在获得如此宽裕的财富之后,继续以同样的价格,甚至以比以前更高的价格出售其商品时,人们可能预计他们的利润会非常大;而且某些个人的利润可能已经如此。 然而,总的来说,我完全有理由相信,他们不是那样的。 这种慷慨的通常效果是,鼓励鲁莽的承业者冒险从事他们不了解的事业;以及他们因自己的疏忽和无知而损失的东西,这不仅仅是补偿他们通过政府的最大自由主义而能得到的一切。1750年,根据最初给予30多分的赏金的同一行为,一吨用于鼓励白鹭渔业(23d Geo). 二、导 言 在14年的时间里,他们每购买100英镑,并付给社会股票,每年有权领取3英镑,由海关总署署长以相当于半年的付款支付。 除了这个伟大的公司,其州长和董事的住所将在伦敦,它被宣布为合法,可以在王国所有不同的港口建立不同的渔业室,条件是每个港口的资本拥有不少于10 000英镑的股份,由它自己承担风险管理,并为了自己的利得和损失。 这些下级商会的贸易与大公司的贸易同样享有年金和各种鼓励。 大公司的订阅很快被填满,在王国的不同出港处建立了几个不同的渔场. 尽管受到所有这些鼓励,但几乎所有的大小公司都失去了其首都的全部或大部分;其中任何一家现在都很少留下遗迹,白鲸渔业现在完全或几乎完全由私人冒险者经营。

p35.original: If any particular manufacture was necessary, indeed, for the defence of the society, it might not always be prudent to depend upon our neighbours for the supply; and if such manufacture could not otherwise be supported at home, it might not be unreasonable that all the other branches of industry should be taxed in order to support it. The bounties upon the exportation of British made sail-cloth, and British made gunpowder, may, perhaps, both be vindicated upon this principle.
p35.zh: 如果任何特定的制造对于捍卫社会来说确实是必要的,那么依赖我们的邻国来供应可能并不总是审慎的;如果这种制造不能在国内得到支持,那么对工业的所有其他分支征税以支持这种生产可能并非不合理。英国制造的帆布和英国制造的火药出口的丰收也许都符合这一原则。

p36.original: But though it can very seldom be reasonable to tax the industry of the great body of the people, in order to support that of some particular class of manufacturers; yet, in the wantonness of great prosperity, when the public enjoys a greater revenue than it knows well what to do with, to give such bounties to favourite manufactures, may, perhaps, be as natural as to incur any other idle expense. In public, as well as in private expenses, great wealth, may, perhaps, frequently be admitted as an apology for great folly. But there must surely be something more than ordinary absurdity in continuing such profusion in times of general difficulty and distress.
p36.zh: 但是,虽然对人民伟大身体的产业征税是很少合理的,以便支持某些特定类别的制造商的产业;然而,在巨大繁荣的肆无忌惮中,当公众拥有比它知道如何做更多的收入时,给最喜爱的制造品以这种好处或许是自然的,甚至会引发任何其他闲置费用。 在公共和私人开支方面,也许可以经常承认巨额财富是对大愚的道歉。 但是,在普遍困难和痛苦的时期继续这种扩散,肯定有比一般荒谬更多的事情。

p37.original: What is called a bounty, is sometimes no more than a drawback, and, consequently, is not liable to the same objections as what is properly a bounty. The bounty, for example, upon refined sugar exported, may be considered as a drawback of the duties upon the brown and Muscovado sugars, from which it is made; the bounty upon wrought silk exported, a drawback of the duties upon raw and thrown silk imported; the bounty upon gunpowder exported, a drawback of the duties upon brimstone and saltpetre imported. In the language of the customs, those allowances only are called drawbacks which are given upon goods exported in the same form in which they are imported. When that form has been so altered by manufacture of any kind as to come under a new denomination, they are called bounties.
p37.zh: 所谓赏金有时只是缺点,因此不会受到与适当赏金相同的反对。 例如,对出口的精制糖的赏金,可视为对制成的褐色和穆斯科瓦多糖的关税的退让;对出口的丝绸的赏金,对进口的生的和抛的丝绸的税金的退让;对出口的火药的赏金,对进口的金石和盐片的退让。 用海关的语言来说,这些津贴只称为对以进口方式出口的货物的缺点。 如果这种形式因任何一种制造而改变,以致于属于新的名称,则称为 " 丰利 " 。

p38.original: Premiums given by the public to artists and manufacturers, who excel in their particular occupations, are not liable to the same objections as bounties. By encouraging extraordinary dexterity and ingenuity, they serve to keep up the emulation of the workmen actually employed in those respective occupations, and are not considerable enough to turn towards any one of them a greater share of the capital of the country than what would go to it of its own accord. Their tendency is not to overturn the natural balance of employments, but to render the work which is done in each as perfect and complete as possible. The expense of premiums, besides, is very trifling, that of bounties very great. The bounty upon corn alone has sometimes cost the public, in one year, more than £300,000.
p38.zh: 公众给予艺术家和制造商的优待,他们在特定职业上表现优异,不会受到与优待相同的反对. 通过鼓励非凡的节俭和聪明,他们有助于保持实际受雇于这些行业的工人的效仿,不足以使其中任何一个工人比它自己拥有的资本拥有更大的份额。 他们的倾向不是推翻就业的自然平衡,而是使每一个工作都尽可能完美和完整。 此外,保险费开支非常少,而奖金则非常大。光是玉米的赏金有时就花在了公众身上,在一年内,就花费了30万英镑以上。

p39.original: Bounties are sometimes called premiums, as drawbacks are sometimes called bounties. But we must, in all cases, attend to the nature of the thing, without paying any regard to the word.
p39.zh: 补偿有时被称为保险费,因为缺点有时被称为补偿。 但是,在所有情况下,我们必须关注事情的性质,而不考虑这个词。

p40.original: Digression concerning the Corn Trade and Corn Laws.

p41.original: I cannot conclude this chapter concerning bounties, without observing, that the praises which have been bestowed upon the law which establishes the bounty upon the exportation of corn, and upon that system of regulations which is connected with it, are altogether unmerited. A particular examination of the nature of the corn trade, and of the principal British laws which relate to it, will sufficiently demonstrate the truth of this assertion. The great importance of this subject must justify the length of the digression.
p41.zh: 在结束这一章时,我不能不指出,对确定玉米出口的赏金的法律以及与此有关的各种规章的赞扬是完全没有道理的。具体审查玉米贸易的性质以及与此有关的英国主要法律,将充分表明这一说法的真实性。这一主题的极端重要性必须成为长期分裂的理由。

p42.original: The trade of the corn merchant is composed of four different branches, which, though they may sometimes be all carried on by the same person, are, in their own nature, four separate and distinct trades. These are, first, the trade of the inland dealer; secondly, that of the merchant-importer for home consumption; thirdly, that of the merchant-exporter of home produce for foreign consumption; and, fourthly, that of the merchant-carrier, or of the importer of corn, in order to export it again.
p42.zh: 玉米商的贸易由四个不同的分支组成,虽然它们有时可能都由同一个人进行,但从其本身的性质来看,是四个独立的和独特的贸易.它们是:第一,内陆经销商的贸易;第二,供家庭消费的商进口商的贸易;第三,供国外消费的家产的商出口商的贸易;第四,供国外消费的商进口商或玉米进口商的贸易,以便再次出口。

p43.original: I. The interest of the inland dealer, and that of the great body of the people, how opposite soever they may at first appear, are, even in years of the greatest scarcity, exactly the same. It is his interest to raise the price of his corn as high as the real scarcity of the season requires, and it can never be his interest to raise it higher. By raising the price, he discourages the consumption, and puts every body more or less, but particularly the inferior ranks of people, upon thrift and good management If, by raising it too high, he discourages the consumption so much that the supply of the season is likely to go beyond the consumption of the season, and to last for some time after the next crop begins to come in, he runs the hazard, not only of losing a considerable part of his corn by natural causes, but of being obliged to sell what remains of it for much less than what he might have had for it several months before. If, by not raising the price high enough, he discourages the consumption so little, that the supply of the season is likely to fall short of the consumption of the season, he not only loses a part of the profit which he might otherwise have made, but he exposes the people to suffer before the end of the season, instead of the hardships of a dearth, the dreadful horrors of a famine. It is the interest of the people that their daily, weekly, and monthly consumption should be proportioned as exactly as possible to the supply of the season. The interest of the inland corn dealer is the same. By supplying them, as nearly as he can judge, in this proportion, he is likely to sell all his corn for the highest price, and with the greatest profit; and his knowledge of the state of the crop, and of his daily, weekly, and monthly sales, enables him to judge, with more or less accuracy, how far they really are supplied in this manner. Without intending the interest of the people, he is necessarily led, by a regard to his own interest, to treat them, even in years of scarcity, pretty much in the same manner as the prudent master of a vessel is sometimes obliged to treat his crew. When he foresees that provisions are likely to run short, he puts them upon short allowance. Though from excess of caution he should sometimes do this without any real necessity, yet all the inconveniencies which his crew can thereby suffer are inconsiderable, in comparison of the danger, misery, and ruin, to which they might sometimes be exposed by a less provident conduct. Though, from excess of avarice, in the same manner, the inland corn merchant should sometimes raise the price of his corn somewhat higher than the scarcity of the season requires, yet all the inconveniencies which the people can suffer from this conduct, which effectually secures them from a famine in the end of the season, are inconsiderable, in comparison of what they might have been exposed to by a more liberal way of dealing in the beginning of it the corn merchant himself is likely to suffer the most by this excess of avarice; not only from the indignation which it generally excites against him, but, though he should escape the effects of this indignation, from the quantity of corn which it necessarily leaves upon his hands in the end of the season, and which, if the next season happens to prove favourable, he must always sell for a much lower price than he might otherwise have had.
p43.zh: 我从你那得到的。内河经销商的利益,以及人民伟大身体的利益,无论他们一开始可能出现什么对立面,即使在最稀少的岁月里,也是完全一样的. 他的兴趣是将他的玉米价格提高到本季真正稀缺需要的水平,而提高玉米价格永远不能成为他的兴趣. 通过提高价格,他劝阻消费,使每一具身体,特别是低等阶层的人,在节俭和良好的管理下,如果通过提高价格,他劝阻消费,以致于供应量可能超出季节的消费,并在下一个作物开始进入之后持续一段时间,他承担着危险,不仅因为自然原因损失了相当一部分的玉米,而且被迫出售剩余的玉米,其价格远远低于他几个月前可能拥有的玉米。 如果由于提价不够高,他劝阻消费如此之少,以致本季的供给量可能低于本季的消费,那么他不仅失去了他原本可能赚到的部分利润,反而暴露了人民在本季结束前遭受的苦难,而不是缺乏的艰辛,可怕的饥荒的恐怖.人民的利益是,他们的日、周、月消费应尽量与季节供应量成正比。内陆玉米经销商的兴趣也一样. 通过提供,几乎他能判断的,按这个比例,他有可能以最高的价格出售他所有的玉米,并获得最大的利润;他了解作物状况,以及他的日、周、月销售情况,使他可以或多或少地准确地判断这种玉米真正供应的程度。 他不必顾及人民的利益,他必然出于自身的利益,即使在匮乏的岁月里,也不得不以与船只的谨慎主人有时有义务对待船员同样的方式对待他们。 当他预见到经费可能短缺时,他给这些经费提供短额津贴。 虽然他有时在没有任何实际必要的情况下应过分谨慎行事,但与危险、痛苦和毁灭相比,他的船员因此可能遭受的所有不便有时会因不那么神圣的行为而面临危险、痛苦和毁灭。 虽然由于过度贪婪,内陆玉米商有时应该以同样的方式提高他的玉米价格,比这个季节的稀缺性需要的要高一些,但是,由于这种行为,人们可能感到不便,实际上使他们在季节结束时免于饥荒,但是,与他们可能由于一开始较自由的经营方式而接触到的相比,这些玉米商本身可能遭受最大的损失;不仅因为这种贪婪的过度,它一般对他感到愤怒,而且,尽管他应该摆脱这种愤慨的影响,但是,由于这一季节结束时它必然留给他手中的玉米数量,而且如果下一季节发生有利的情况,他必须始终以比他本来要低得多的价格出售。

p44.original: Were it possible, indeed, for one great company of merchants to possess themselves of the whole crop of an extensive country, it might perhaps be their interest to deal with it, as the Dutch are said to do with the spiceries of the Moluccas, to destroy or throw away a considerable part of it, in order to keep up the price of the rest. But it is scarce possible, even by the violence of law, to establish such an extensive monopoly with regard to corn; and wherever the law leaves the trade free, it is of all commodities the least liable to be engrossed or monopolized by the forced a few large capitals, which buy up the greater part of it. Not only its value far exceeds what the capitals of a few private men are capable of purchasing; but, supposing they were capable of purchasing it, the manner in which it is produced renders this purchase altogether impracticable. As, in every civilized country, it is the commodity of which the annual consumption is the greatest; so a greater quantity of industry is annually employed in producing corn than in producing any other commodity. When it first comes from the ground, too, it is necessarily divided among a greater number of owners than any other commodity; and these owners can never be collected into one place, like a number of independent manufacturers, but are necessarily scattered through all the different corners of the country. These first owners either immediately supply the consumers in their own neighbourhood, or they supply other inland dealers, who supply those consumers. The inland dealers in corn, therefore, including both the farmer and the baker, are necessarily more numerous than the dealers in any other commodity; and their dispersed situation renders it altogether impossible for them to enter into any general combination. If, in a year of scarcity, therefore, any of them should find that he had a good deal more corn upon hand than, at the current price, he could hope to dispose of before the end of the season, he would never think of keeping up this price to his own loss, and to the sole benefit of his rivals and competitors, but would immediately lower it, in order to get rid of his corn before the new crop began to come in. The same motives, the same interests, which would thus regulate the conduct of any one dealer, would regulate that of every other, and oblige them all in general to sell their corn at the price which, according to the best of their judgment, was most suitable to the scarcity or plenty of the season.
p44.zh: 如果,事实上,如果一个伟大的商人公司能够占有一个广大国家的全部作物,也许他们有兴趣处理,因为据说荷兰人对摩鹿加人的香料负责,摧毁或丢掉其中相当一部分,以便维持其余的粮食价格。 但是,即使通过法律暴力,也几乎不可能对玉米建立如此广泛的垄断;只要法律使贸易自由,它就最不可能被几个强势的大首都所充斥或垄断,这些首都购买了大部分的玉米。不仅其价值远远超过了几个私人男子的首都能够购买的价值;而且,假设他们有能力购买,那么生产这种价值的方式使得这种购买完全不可行。与每一个文明国家一样,每年消费最多的商品是玉米;因此,每年生产玉米的工业比生产任何其他商品的工业数量要多。 当它刚从地上来的时候,它必然比任何其他商品被更多的所有者分成;这些所有者永远不能被收集到一个地方,就像一些独立的制造商一样,但必然分散在全国各个角落. 这些最初的业主要么立即供应他们自己附近的消费者,要么供应其他内陆经销商,由这些经销商供应这些消费者。 因此,包括农民和面包师在内的内陆玉米经销商必然比任何其他商品的经销商数量更多;他们分散的情况使他们完全不可能进入任何一般的组合。 因此,如果在短缺的一年里,他们中的任何一人会发现他手上的玉米比目前价格要多,他可以希望在季末之前处理掉,那么他就不会想到维持这个价格以弥补自己的损失,并且只为了对手和竞争对手的利益,而是会立刻降低这个价格,以便在新作物开始出现之前摆脱他的玉米.同样的动机和利益将因此规范任何一个经销商的行为,将规范每一个经销商的行为,并迫使他们普遍以价格出售玉米,而根据他们的判断,价格最适合季节的稀缺或丰厚。

p45.original: Whoever examines, with attention, the history of the dearths and famines which have afflicted any part of Europe during either the course of the present or that of the two preceding centuries, of several of which we have pretty exact accounts, will find, I believe, that a dearth never has arisen from any combination among the inland dealers in corn, nor from any other cause but a real scarcity, occasioned sometimes, perhaps, and in some particular places, by the waste of war, but in by far the greatest number of cases by the fault of the seasons; and that a famine has never arisen from any other cause but the violence of government attempting, by improper means, to remedy the inconveniencies of a dearth.
p45.zh: 我认为,无论谁仔细研究一下欧洲任何地区在目前或前两个世纪中遭受的匮乏和饥荒的历史,我们有相当准确的叙述,谁都会发现,贫困从未产生于内陆玉米交易商之间的任何结合,也从未产生于其他任何原因,但真正的匮乏有时、也许,在某些特定的地方,是由于战争的浪费,但迄今为止,最大的案例是季节的过错;饥荒从未产生于任何其他原因,只有政府的暴力试图以不正当手段弥补匮乏者的不便。

p46.original: In an extensive corn country, between all the different parts of which there is a free commerce and communication, the scarcity occasioned by the most unfavourable seasons can never be so great as to produce a famine; and the scantiest crop, if managed with frugality and economy, will maintain, through the year, the same number of people that are commonly fed in a more affluent manner by one of moderate plenty. The seasons most unfavourable to the crop are those of excessive drought or excessive rain. But as corn grows equally upon high and low lands, upon grounds that are disposed to be too wet, and upon those that are disposed to be too dry, either the drought or the rain, which is hurtful to one part of the country, is favourable to another; and though, both in the wet and in the dry season, the crop is a good deal less than in one more properly tempered; yet, in both, what is lost in one part of the country is in some measure compensated by what is gained in the other. In rice countries, where the crop not only requires a very moist soil, but where, in a certain period of its growing, it must be laid under water, the effects of a drought are much more dismal. Even in such countries, however, the drought is, perhaps, scarce ever so universal as necessarily to occasion a famine, if the government would allow a free trade. The drought in Bengal, a few years ago, might probably have occasioned a very great dearth. Some improper regulations, some injudicious restraints, imposed by the servants of the East India Company upon the rice trade, contributed, perhaps, to turn that dearth into a famine.
p46.zh: 在一个广阔的玉米国家,在商业和通信自由的所有地区之间,最不利的季节造成的稀缺程度永远不可能达到造成饥荒的程度;而最贫瘠的作物,如果以节俭和节约的方式管理,将维持一年中通常由中等富足者以更富裕的方式供养的人数。 对作物最不利的季节是过度干旱或过度降雨。 但是,由于玉米在高低土地上同样生长,其土壤被处理得太湿,其土壤被处理太干,干旱或雨水对一个国家造成伤害,对另一个土地有利;虽然在湿润和旱季,作物的产量比在更适当温和的作物少;然而,在这两种情况下,一个国家一个土地的损失在某种程度上都得到另一个土地所得的补偿。 在水稻国,作物不仅需要湿润的土壤,而且在生长的某一时期,必须将其埋在水下,干旱的影响就更令人沮丧。 然而,即使在这些国家,如果政府允许自由贸易,旱灾可能也很少发生,以致必然发生饥荒。孟加拉的干旱,几年前, 可能已经造成非常的匮乏。东印度公司的佣人对稻米贸易施加了一些不适当的规定,一些有害的限制,也许促成了将这种匮乏变成饥荒。

p47.original: When the government, in order to remedy the inconveniencies of a dearth, orders all the dealers to sell their corn at what it supposes a reasonable price, it either hinders them from bringing it to market, which may sometimes produce a famine even in the beginning of the season; or, if they bring it thither, it enables the people, and thereby encourages them to consume it so fast as must necessarily produce a famine before the end of the season. The unlimited, unrestrained freedom of the corn trade, as it is the only effectual preventive of the miseries of a famine, so it is the best palliative of the inconveniencies of a dearth; for the inconveniencies of a real scarcity cannot be remedied; they can only be palliated. No trade deserves more the full protection of the law, and no trade requires it so much; because no trade is so much exposed to popular odium.
p47.zh: 当政府为了弥补缺粮的不便,命令所有经销商以它所认为的合理价格出售玉米时,它要么阻碍他们将玉米带入市场,这有时甚至在季节开始时也会造成饥荒;要么,如果他们带来饥荒,就能使人民得以生存,从而鼓励他们如此迅速地食用玉米,在季节结束前必然会产生饥荒.玉米贸易不受限制和不受限制的自由,因为这是对饥荒灾难的唯一有效预防,因此,它是对缺乏粮食者不方便的最佳缓解;因为缺乏粮食者不方便是无法补救的;它们只能被调和。 没有哪个贸易应该受到法律的充分保护,没有哪个贸易需要这样多;因为没有哪个贸易受到如此多的流行的碘的污染。

p48.original: In years of scarcity, the inferior ranks of people impute their distress to the avarice of the corn merchant, who becomes the object of their hatred and indignation. Instead of making profit upon such occasions, therefore, he is often in danger of being utterly ruined, and of having his magazines plundered and destroyed by their violence. It is in years of scarcity, however, when prices are high, that the corn merchant expects to make his principal profit. He is generally in contract with some farmers to furnish him, for a certain number of years, with a certain quantity of corn, at a certain price. This contract price is settled according to what is supposed to be the moderate and reasonable, that is, the ordinary or average price, which, before the late years of scarcity, was commonly about 28s. for the quarter of wheat, and for that of other grain in proportion. In years of scarcity, therefore, the corn merchant buys a great part of his corn for the ordinary price, and sells it for a much higher. That this extraordinary profit, however, is no more than sufficient to put his trade upon a fair level with other trades, and to compensate the many losses which he sustains upon other occasions, both from the perishable nature of the commodity itself, and from the frequent and unforeseen fluctuations of its price, seems evident enough, from this single circumstance, that great fortunes are as seldom made in this as in any other trade. The popular odium, however, which attends it in years of scarcity, the only years in which it can be very profitable, renders people of character and fortune averse to enter into it. It is abandoned to an inferior set of dealers; and millers, bakers, meal-men, and meal-factors, together with a number of wretched hucksters, are almost the only middle people that, in the home market, come between the grower and the consumer.
p48.zh: 在匮乏的岁月中,低等阶层的人把他们的痛苦归结为玉米商的贪婪,而玉米商成了他们的仇恨和愤慨的对象。 因此,他不是在这种场合赚钱,而是经常面临被彻底摧毁的危险,他的杂志被其暴力掠夺和毁坏的危险。 然而,当价格高涨时,玉米商正是在缺乏资金的年代里期望着能够赚取他的主要利润。 他一般与一些农民签订合同,以一定的价格给他提供一定数量的玉米,为期一定年. 这种合同价格是按照一般的温和合理价格,即普通价格或平均价格来结算的,在短缺的晚年以前,小麦的季度通常约为28s,而其他谷物的价格则按比例计算。 因此,在多年的匮乏中,玉米商以普通价格购买了他的一大部分玉米,并以高得多的价格出售. 然而,这一特别利润不足以使他与其他贸易的贸易达到公平水平,并足以补偿他在其他情况下承受的许多损失,这些损失既来自商品本身的易腐化性质,也来自其价格经常和意外波动,从这种单一情况来看,似乎足够明显,在这方面,财富与任何其他贸易一样少见。 然而,流行的碘酸盐,在稀缺的岁月里,也就是它能够非常有利可图的年月里,却让品格和财富的人不愿进入它。 它被抛弃给一群低劣的商人;而磨坊主、面包师、餐工和饭菜人,以及一些可怜的哈克人,几乎是唯一在家庭市场里,在种植者和消费者之间出现的中间人物。

p49.original: The ancient policy of Europe, instead of discountenancing this popular odium against a trade so beneficial to the public, seems, on the contrary, to have authorised and encouraged it.
p49.zh: 相反,欧洲古老的政策并没有淡化这种对公众有利的贸易的流行气味,反而似乎授权并鼓励了这种贸易。

p50.original: By the 5th and 6th of Edward VI cap. 14, it was enacted, that whoever should buy any corn or grain, with intent to sell it again, should be reputed an unlawful engrosser, and should, for the first fault, suffer two months imprisonment, and forfeit the value of the corn; for the second, suffer six months imprisonment, and forfeit double the value; and, for the third, be set in the pillory, suffer imprisonment during the king's pleasure, and forfeit all his goods and chattels. The ancient policy of most other parts of Europe was no better than that of England.
p50.zh: 到了爱德华六世的第五和第六座封顶.14,颁布规定,凡购买任何玉米或谷物,意图再次出售的,均应被誉为非法的占卜者,并因第一种过错,应处以两个月的监禁,并没收玉米的价值;第二种情况下,应处以六个月的监禁,并没收其价值的两倍;第三种情况下,应处以平底币,在国王的享乐期间,处以监禁,并没收其所有货物和动产. 欧洲大多数其他地区的古老政策并不比英格兰好.

p51.original: Our ancestors seem to have imagined, that the people would buy their corn cheaper of the farmer than of the corn merchant, who, they were afraid, would require, over and above the price which he paid to the farmer, an exorbitant profit to himself. They endeavoured, therefore, to annihilate his trade altogether. They even endeavoured to hinder, as much as possible, any middle man of any kind from coming in between the grower and the consumer; and this was the meaning of the many restraints which they imposed upon the trade of those whom they called kidders, or carriers of corn; a trade which nobody was allowed to exercise without a licence, ascertaining his qualifications as a man of probity and fair dealing. The authority of three justices of the peace was, by the statute of Edward VI. necessary in order to grant this licence. But even this restraint was afterwards thought insufficient, and, by a statute of Elizabeth, the privilege of granting it was confined to the quarter-sessions.
p51.zh: 我们的祖先们似乎想象,人民会比玉米商更便宜地购买他们的玉米,他们害怕,他们要求,除了他向农民支付的价格外,他们自己还要获得高额利润。 因此,他们试图彻底消灭他的贸易。 他们甚至尽量阻挠任何中间人物进入种植者和消费者之间;这就是他们对他们称之为小贩或玉米携带者的贸易施加的许多限制的含义;这种贸易没有许可证就不允许任何人进行,从而确定他是否有资格从事正直和公平交易。 根据爱德华六世的规约,三名治安官的权力是颁发这一许可证所必需的。 但是,即使这种约束在事后也被认为是不够的,根据伊丽莎白的法规,授予它的特权仅限于季度会议.

p52.original: The ancient policy of Europe endeavoured, in this manner, to regulate agriculture, the great trade of the country, by maxims quite different from those which it established with regard to manufactures, the great trade of the towns. By leaving a farmer no other customers but either the consumers or their immediate factors, the kidders and carriers of corn, it endeavoured to force him to exercise the trade, not only of a farmer, but of a corn merchant, or corn retailer. On the contrary, it, in many cases, prohibited the manufacturer from exercising the trade of a shopkeeper, or from selling his own goods by retail. It meant, by the one law, to promote the general interest of the country, or to render corn cheap, without, perhaps, its being well understood how this was to be done. By the other, it meant to promote that of a particular order of men, the shopkeepers, who would be so much undersold by the manufacturer, it was supposed, that their trade would be ruined, if he was allowed to retail at all.
p52.zh: 欧洲古代的政策就是以这种方式管理农业,即国家的伟大贸易,其宗旨与它确定的制造、城镇的伟大贸易大相径庭。 它使农民除了消费者或其直接因素之外没有其他顾客、玉米的幼童和携带者,试图迫使他不仅从事农民,而且从事玉米商或玉米零售商的贸易。 相反,在许多情况下,它禁止制造商从事店主的贸易,或通过零售出售自己的货物。 根据一项法律,这意味着促进国家的普遍利益,或使玉米价格低廉,而也许人们并不完全了解如何做到这一点。另一种说法是,如果允许他零售的话,它的意思是宣传一个特定的男人的秩序,即店主,他们被制造商卖得如此少,这应该是他们的贸易被破坏的。

p53.original: The manufacturer, however, though he had been allowed to keep a shop, and to sell his own goods by retail, could not have undersold the common shopkeeper. Whatever part of his capital he might have placed in his shop, he must have withdrawn it from his manufacture. In order to carry on his business on a level with that of other people, as he must have had the profit of a manufacturer on the one part, so he must have had that of a shopkeeper upon the other. Let us suppose, for example, that in the particular town where he lived, ten per cent. was the ordinary profit both of manufacturing and shopkeeping stock; he must in this case have charged upon every piece of his own goods, which he sold in his shop, a profit of twenty per cent. When he carried them from his workhouse to his shop, he must have valued them at the price for which he could have sold them to a dealer or shopkeeper, who would have bought them by wholesale. If he valued them lower, he lost a part of the profit of his manufacturing capital. When, again, he sold them from his shop, unless he got the same price at which a shopkeeper would have sold them, he lost a part of the profit of his shop-keeping capital. Though he might appear, therefore, to make a double profit upon the same piece of goods, yet, as these goods made successively a part of two distinct capitals, he made but a single profit upon the whole capital employed about them; and if he made less than his profit, he was a loser, and did not employ his whole capital with the same advantage as the greater part of his neighbours.
p53.zh: 然而,虽然允许制造商保留一家商店和通过零售出售自己的货物,但不能将普通店主卖掉。 不管他把哪部分的资本放在他的店里 他一定把它从他的制造中撤出了 为了与他人在某种程度上继续经营,因为他一方面一定有制造商的利润,所以他另一方面一定有店主的利润. 例如,让我们假设,在他居住的特定城镇,10%是制造业和商店库存的普通利润;在这种情况下,他必须收取他自己在商店出售的每件货物的费用,利润为20%。 当他从工作室把货运到他的店铺时,他必须按他本来可以卖给一个经销商或店主的价格来估价这些货款,因为店主本来可以批发地购买这些货款。 如果他轻轻地看重它们,他失去了一部分制造资本的利润.之后,他又从他的店里卖了这些东西,除非他得到一个店主本来会卖掉的一样的价格,否则他失去了他店主资本的一部分利润. 因此,虽然他似乎在同一件货物上获得双重利润,但是,由于这些货物相继成为两个不同首都的一部分,他只为所雇用的全部资本谋取了单一利润;如果他的利润少于他的利润,他就是一个失败者,而且没有利用他的全部资本,其优势与其邻居的较大部分相同。

p54.original: What the manufacturer was prohibited to do, the farmer was in some measure enjoined to do; to divide his capital between two different employments; to keep one part of it in his granaries and stack-yard, for supplying the occasional demands of the market, and to employ the other in the cultivation of his land. But as he could not afford to employ the latter for less than the ordinary profits of farming stock, so he could as little afford to employ the former for less than the ordinary profits of mercantile stock. Whether the stock which really carried on the business of a corn merchant belonged to the person who was called a farmer, or to the person who was called a corn merchant, an equal profit was in both cases requisite, in order to indemnify its owner for employing it in this manner, in order to put his business on a level with other trades, and in order to hinder him from having an interest to change it as soon as possible for some other. The farmer, therefore, who was thus forced to exercise the trade of a corn merchant, could not afford to sell his corn cheaper than any other corn merchant would have been obliged to do in the case of a free competition.
p54.zh: 制造商被禁止从事的,在某种程度上,农民被责令从事;将资本分为两种不同的职业;将一部分留在他的粮仓和堆场,供应市场偶尔的需求,并雇用另一部分用于耕种他的土地。 但是,由于他不能以低于农业库存的普通利润来雇用后者,因此他也几乎没有能力以低于商业库存的普通利润来雇用前者。无论是真正经营玉米商生意的股票属于被称作农民的人,还是被称作玉米商的人,在这两种情况下都必须获得同等利润,以补偿其所有者以这种方式雇用玉米商,使其生意与其他行业处于一个水平,并阻止他尽快为其他行业改变其利益。 因此,被迫从事玉米商人贸易的农民无力支付出售其玉米的费用,比其他任何玉米商人在自由竞争的情况下必须出售的玉米要便宜。

p55.original: The dealer who can employ his whole stock in one single branch of business, has an advantage of the same kind with the workman who can employ his whole labour in one single operation. As the latter acquires a dexterity which enables him, with the same two hands, to perform a much greater quantity of work, so the former acquires so easy and ready a method of transacting his business, of buying and disposing of his goods, that with the same capital he can transact a much greater quantity of business.
